source.title: LoRA Training in the NTK Regime has No Spurious Local Minima
source.authors: Uijeong Jang; J. Lee; Ernest K. Ryu

record.file_problem: not stated; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes whether gradient-based LoRA training avoids spurious local minima, using a different setting and rank condition from the two-layer teacher-student width comparisons in V2.
record.gate_note: The paper's theorem is a result on spurious local minima. Training-curve results report training loss, not training classification error, so they do not establish V1. Theoretical rank and dataset-size conditions are not separate outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves a landscape result for low-rank adaptation of linearized pre-trained models. It does not test V2's two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks, frequency of convergence to spurious minima, or student-width advantage. LoRA rank is a different parameter from student neuron count. Its experiments and other theoretical results do not test V1 or V3–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' interpretation. More precisely, the theorem excludes spurious local minima for a generically perturbed NTK LoRA objective at sufficient rank; it does not directly cover deterministic P=0. The corollary bounds the unperturbed regularized objective gap, and the gradient-method argument is conditional on convergence under the cited assumptions. Experiments report matching final losses and faster convergence with higher rank or full fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies LoRA fine-tuning of pre-trained models in the NTK regime, with a rank condition and a perturbed loss; V2 describes two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and student-neuron count.
record.method_sensitivity: The theoretical guarantee depends on LoRA rank relative to KN and on a generic nonzero perturbation; the authors state that lower LoRA rank or using full fine-tuning changes convergence rate in their experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the NTK approximation, when r(r+1)/2 > KN and a global optimum exists, almost every nonzero positive-semidefinite perturbation makes all LoRA second-order stationary points globally optimal. A sufficiently small perturbation also bounds the unperturbed regularized objective gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficient LoRA rank eliminates spurious local minima of a generically perturbed linearized fine-tuning objective.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that linearized NLP, image, and speech fine-tuning runs reach the same loss, while higher LoRA rank and full fine-tuning converge faster.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing LoRA rank can accelerate loss convergence in linearized fine-tuning of pre-trained models.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The no-spurious-minima theorem applies to a perturbed loss; the paper explicitly says it does not apply directly when practical training sets P=0. Experiments fine-tune linearized pre-trained models and report training-loss curves, not direct counts of spurious minima or training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No other outcome rows for the tested version. The NLP, image, and speech training curves report loss convergence and differing rates, but do not measure spurious local minima or V2's teacher-student width relationship. Test-accuracy results do not bear on the versions tested.

untested.parts: Training classification error of randomly initialized convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels.
All parts: two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, increasing matched widths, and the effect of one or two extra student neurons on convergence to spurious minima.
Depth degradation in plain networks and its prevention through residual shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, and initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth.
Loss recovery, curvature changes, and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source, but no verdict is warranted because none of the supplied claim versions is tested. Experimental convergence results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test random initialization or report training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 or corrupted labels.

It does not test two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, jointly growing teacher and student widths, or giving the student one or two neurons more than the teacher; it studies LoRA rank in the NTK regime instead.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison or normalization ablation.
No initialization comparison or depth sweep for plain networks.
No learning-rate stability-limit or sharpness experiment.

rows.subject: LoRA fine-tuning in the NTK regime
rows.size_stated: LoRA rank r satisfying r(r+1)/2 > KN; N training data points and K-dimensional outputs
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 4.1 states that, for almost all nonzero positive-semidefinite perturbations P, all second-order stationary points of the perturbed LoRA loss are global minimizers; Corollary 4.2 gives an epsilon-approximation guarantee for the unperturbed objective.
rows.measure: Whether second-order stationary points are global minimizers; closeness of the unperturbed empirical risk to its minimum.
rows.value: All SOSPs of L̂λ,P are global minimizers for almost all nonzero P; the unperturbed empirical risk is ε-close to its minimum.
rows.uncertainty: Theorem 4.1 states probability 1 with respect to Lebesgue measure; Corollary 4.2 states an ε bound.
rows.note: The guarantee is for a perturbed loss. The paper says Theorem 4.1 does not apply directly to the practical setup with deterministic P=0, though it interprets the result as showing generic absence of spurious local minima.
rows.check: The theorem is correctly reported as a LoRA landscape guarantee, but it cannot establish V2's teacher-student width effect. Include the assumption that the unperturbed regularized objective has a global minimizer. Corollary 4.2 bounds the unperturbed regularized objective gap by 2ε times the nuclear norm of an optimum; it does not generally guarantee an ε gap in unregularized empirical risk or unconditional convergence of gradient descent.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LoRA in the NTK regime with r(r+1)/2 > KN and almost all nonzero positive-semidefinite perturbations
reader_labels.reason: Theorem 4.1 rules out spurious SOSPs under these conditions, and Corollary 4.2 bounds the unperturbed empirical-risk gap (R1). This does not test the version's teacher-student width comparisons.
